abstract.t: A fixture, not a specification: CRC-32 and Adler-32 over a window of a buffer, as nish's std checksum takes them, from spec to a run of the fixture module in tests/fixtures/checksum-window. Each function takes its bytes as (buf, off, len), which the interface declares as one bytes parameter.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

The module is the fixture checksum of tests/fixtures/checksum-window/fixture, run with --package fixture=tests/fixtures/checksum-window/fixture. It passes each call to nish/compress/checksum. A copy in broken/ reads its window from the start of the buffer, which the same contract refuses: the emitted test passes every window at a nonzero offset, between guard bytes.

section.name: Interface
section.sourcecode: // module: fixture/checksum export const crc32 = (buf: u8[] /* window */): u32 export const adler32 = (buf: u8[] /* window */): u32 export const adler32Update = (adler: u32, buf: u8[] /* window */): u32

section.name: CRC-32
section.t: crc32 MUST return the CRC-32 of the window's bytes, the reflected CRC with polynomial 0xEDB88320 that zlib computes, and only of those bytes.

section.name: Adler-32
section.t: adler32 MUST return the Adler-32 of the window's bytes, as zlib computes it, and only of those bytes.
adler32Update MUST return the Adler-32 of the bytes an earlier checksum covered followed by the window's bytes.
section.sourcecode: // P-ADLER32-SPLIT covers R-ADLER32, R-ADLER32-UPDATE — a checksum continued over a second window is the checksum of both forall (a: u8[] /* 0..32 */, b: u8[] /* 0..32 */) => adler32Update(adler32(a), b) === adler32(a.concat(b))

section.name: Check values
section.t: These values are what zlib's crc32 and adler32 print in Python 3, as python3 -c 'import zlib; print(zlib.crc32(b"123456789"))' does.
The CRC-32 of "123456789" is Check = 3421780262, and of "" it is Zero = 0.
The Adler-32 of "Wikipedia" is Adler = 300286872, and of "" it is Initial = 1.
The Adler-32 of "abc" continued from Start = 300286872 is Continued = 519570622.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: Neither checksum resists a deliberate change: both detect accidental errors only.

front.title: Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels

abstract.t: In many standards track documents several words are used to signify the requirements in the specification. These words are often capitalized. This document defines these words as they should be interpreted in IETF documents. This document specifies an Internet Best Current Practices for the Internet Community, and requests discussion and suggestions for improvements.

front.title: Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words

abstract.t: RFC 2119 specifies common key words that may be used in protocol specifications. This document aims to reduce the ambiguity by clarifying that only UPPERCASE usage of the key words have the defined special meanings.
